text:
Maya Patel: Heads-up — customer acme-inc reported a surge of 429s this morning after a new client rollout. They noticed the JS SDK retried aggressively and ended up creating duplicate resources and an unexpected billing increase. Logs attached.

Alex Chen: Can you paste the error payload and confirm SDK version? Are they setting idempotency headers on create calls?

Maya Patel: They're on redwood-js@1.3.0 (released last month). No idempotency header in their calls — legacy codepath. Error sample: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 18
{"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":120}
```

Priya Singh: Two cascaded issues here: (1) client defaults allow several retry attempts with minimal spacing and no jitter; (2) server quota window is small so concurrent retries reflood the pool. Immediate mitigations: cap client-side retries and switch to exponential backoff with full jitter. Example suggested config (recommend 2 retries max):
```
retry: {
  maxRetries: 2,
  baseDelayMs: 200,
  maxDelayMs: 2000,
  strategy: 'exponentialWithFullJitter'
}
```
Also require `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` for POSTs that create billable resources.

Jin Park: Support action plan: (A) Ask customer to upgrade to 1.3.1 with the new retry defaults; (B) Server side: detect burst and extend `retry_after` to give clients time to back off; (C) Apply temporary quota smoothing for the account to avoid refill-driven bursts.

Alex Chen: On the SDK side I'm proposing a changelist: reduce default `maxRetries` from 5 -> 2, enable full jitter by default, and add a middleware to warn (non-fatal) when high-risk endpoints are called without an Idempotency-Key. We'll also add docs showing safe retry patterns.

Maya Patel: Repro steps I used locally to trigger the pattern:
1) k6 script: fire 200 concurrent POSTs over ~6s to `/v1/ops/create`
2) Do NOT set idempotency header
3) Observe 429s then clients retry and produce repeated 201 responses in server logs (duplicate creates)

k6 snippet:
```
import http from 'k6/http';
export default function() {
  http.post('https://api.redwood.ai/v1/ops/create', JSON.stringify({name:'x'}), { headers: {'Content-Type':'application/json'} });
}
```

Priya Singh: For customer remediation, check billing ledger for duplicate invoice items and issue credits if we find duplicates. Also recommend they instrument idempotency on create endpoints.

incidents-bot: Incident created: INC-2024-492 — tagging eng-runtime, eng-ml, and billing.

Alex Chen: I'll draft the SDK patch (branch: sdk/retry-defaults-reduce) and a short ops runbook for immediate mitigation. Priya — can you lead customer comms and credit decision? Maya — please attach full request-id traces.

Maya Patel: On it. Attaching traces now: r-11a2, r-11a3, r-11a7. Also leaving a note to the customer with the suggested temporary client config.

Jin Park: Follow-ups: add a telemetry metric `retry_induced_success_count` (successes after client retry attempts) and build a dashboard to detect thundering-herd patterns (spike in retry_induced_success + drop in rate-limit-remaining).

Maya Patel: One more thought — we could add a server-side `burst_suppress` flag per account. If set, server will hold on to accept windows for small random delays to smooth incoming refill bursts. Would need careful rollout.

Alex Chen: Agree — that could be a safe mitigation while we push SDK changes. We'll schedule a short spike-detection prototype.

Maya Patel: Thanks all :sparkles: I'll update this thread once the customer upgrades or we have a patch validated.
